rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2.2 and Section 3 - the authors sampled 210 points at five depths in four seasons (autumn 2015 to spring 2017), measured ECe of saturation extracts and built their own 3-D kriged salinity maps (Tables 2-3, Figures 4-7).
rows.notes: The study is a primary geostatistical survey of seasonal soil salinity (ECe, 0-150 cm) in irrigated rice fields of the Ili River Valley, Xinjiang (Section 2.1: rice irrigation May-September, surface/flood water application with near-saturated soil water content May-August, Figure 8). Drip irrigation is never tested or mentioned as the irrigation method in the study area; the only link to drip is a cited reference (ref. 2) on a mulched drip-irrigated cotton field. The study does show that salt accumulates from spring to autumn under rice irrigation and that topsoil and deep subsoil ECe are higher, with swales/poorly drained areas most saline, but this is evidence about surface-irrigated paddy fields, not about salinization occurring under drip systems. Hence no own evidence on the technology in the passage.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study concerns surface-irrigated rice paddies with seasonal 3-D salinity mapping; it contains no drip irrigation trial, so it cannot support a claim about salinization under drip beyond a general observation that irrigated fields in semiarid areas accumulate salt.
